Sanjeev AI: Testing Strategy & E2E Validation ​

This document formally defines the testing strategy for core product features before they are implemented by the development team. All features must adhere to Test-Driven Development (TDD) principles.

1. Cloud Video Rendering (Hybrid Export) ​

The video rendering system has two tiers (Local Canvas vs Cloud FFmpeg). E2E tests must validate the user permissions, UI state, and backend logic.

1.1 Frontend E2E Tests (Playwright) ​

  • Test Case 1: Standard User Restrictions
    • Scenario: A user with plan: "free" opens the Export Modal.
    • Expected Outcome: The "Cloud Render" toggle is visible but disabled/locked. Clicking it should trigger an upsell prompt. The resolution dropdown should only show standard options supported by the browser canvas.
  • Test Case 2: Premium User Options
    • Scenario: A user with plan: "pro" opens the Export Modal.
    • Expected Outcome: The user can freely toggle between "Local Render" and "Cloud Render". When Cloud Render is selected, the resolution dropdown displays "720p (Default)" and "1080p".
  • Test Case 3: Concurrent Render Locking
    • Scenario: A user initiates a Local Render.
    • Expected Outcome: The Export button and Cloud Render toggle are immediately disabled to prevent overlapping rendering jobs.

1.2 Backend Unit/Integration Tests (Jest) ​

  • Test Case 1: Credit Validation
    • Scenario: requestCloudRender is called by a premium user with credits: 0.
    • Expected Outcome: The Cloud Function immediately throws an unauthenticated or payment-required HttpsError. No Cloud Run job is dispatched.
  • Test Case 2: Credit Deduction
    • Scenario: requestCloudRender is called by a premium user with credits: 10.
    • Expected Outcome: The Cloud Run job is dispatched successfully, and the user's credit balance is atomically decremented by the calculated cost.
  • Test Case 3: FFmpeg Stitching (Mocked Integration)
    • Scenario: The Cloud Run job container executes the rendering script with a standard test manifest.
    • Expected Outcome: The script successfully outputs an MP4 file, and validates that the output resolution strictly matches the requested 720p or 1080p parameter.

2. In-App Notification System (Global Inbox) ​

The notification system must accurately reflect asynchronous background tasks in real-time.

2.1 Frontend E2E Tests (Playwright) ​

  • Test Case 1: Real-time Inbox Badge Updates
    • Scenario: A new document is written to the user's notifications sub-collection by a background process.
    • Expected Outcome: The notification bell icon in the NavBar immediately increments its unread count badge without requiring a page refresh.
  • Test Case 2: Reading Notifications
    • Scenario: The user opens the notification drawer and clicks on an unread notification.
    • Expected Outcome: The specific notification is marked as read: true in Firestore, the unread badge counter decrements, and the user is navigated to the actionUrl (e.g., the completed video URL).
  • Test Case 3: Edge Case - Failed Render Alerts
    • Scenario: The Cloud Run engine crashes or times out.
    • Expected Outcome: An "error" type notification is pushed to the inbox. The UI must render this notification with an appropriate error styling (e.g., red icon/text) to distinguish it from success messages.

3. URL State Persistence (Batch 2) ​

The Studio must support deep linking and persist active project/script state across hard refreshes via React Router to prevent frustrating kick-backs to the home dashboard.

3.1 Frontend E2E Tests (Playwright) ​

  • Test Case 1: Deep Link Navigation
    • Scenario: A user navigates directly to /studio/:projectId/:scriptId via a bookmarked link or pasted URL.
    • Expected Outcome: The application initializes the Studio directly, loading the correct project and script data without forcing a redirect to the dashboard.
  • Test Case 2: Hard Refresh State Retention
    • Scenario: While actively editing a script in the Studio (/studio/:projectId/:scriptId), the user performs a hard browser refresh (Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + R).
    • Expected Outcome: The Studio re-renders successfully and the exact same project and script remain active. The user is NOT kicked back to the dashboard.
  • Test Case 3: Invalid URL Parameters
    • Scenario: A user navigates to a Studio URL with an invalid or non-existent projectId or scriptId.
    • Expected Outcome: The application gracefully handles the error, showing a user-friendly "Project/Script Not Found" state or safely redirecting to the dashboard instead of crashing.
